{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22, at the dev_reflow2 hub, after a deliberate two-session trial (the hub fixing #571 in a worktree while the owner's session merged #570 and #572): "Interesting, I would have thought it would have been the other way where the design side was frictionless and implemented code had the friction. Can we fix this?" Then: "I prefer to fix things correctly, even if things take longer to do." So this records the CORRECT fix, not a containment.

═══ THE OBSERVATION THAT PROMPTED IT ═══
Code work in parallel was frictionless: separate worktrees and build dirs, zero collisions over ~3 hours. The DESIGN side cost four CI runs and three manual merges:
· the coherence gate refused the branch, because its design changes had gone to the live store (fact:a-worktree-fix-recorded-its-design-changes-in-the-live-store-and-the-branch-gate-failed-2026-09-22);
· GitHub reported CONFLICTING twice, once per sibling merge, because both sides rewrote docs/design/reflow2.json;
· the merge driver's output needed re-exporting (fact:the-merge-driver-writes-the-merged-export-in-a-different-byte-layout-than-the-exporter-2026-09-22);
· exporting mid-merge broke lineage;
· one ChangeEvent written to both the live and a branch-private store conflicted on merge.
This is the same mechanism fact:the-live-graph-does-not-branch-so-two-open-prs-collide has recorded at least seven times since 2026-08-14. The repository's current working rule is to SERIALISE: land the sibling before exporting on a new branch. That rule works by forbidding parallel design work.

═══ THE ROOT CAUSE, AS A CLAIM TO TEST ═══
reflow2 treats the design as ONE LIVE, UNBRANCHED truth, while it records two kinds of fact with different natures:
· INTENT (requirements, decisions, rules, findings, ideas) really is unbranched. It should be seen by every session at once, and the live shared server is right for it.
· IMPLEMENTATION FACTS (an artifact's accepted checksum, the ChangeEvent for a branch's code, a new file's registration, a verification's run against that code) belong to the BRANCH that produced them, exactly as the code does. Recorded in the unbranched store, they (1) land in whichever checkout the store saves into, (2) can't be measured against the branch's files, and (3) leak into sibling branches' exports.

═══ THE FIX, AS ONE CHANGE WITH PARTS THAT BELONG TOGETHER (options inside each part, none chosen) ═══
① THE SERVER KNOWS EACH SESSION'S WORKTREE AND BRANCH. A session declares its working root, or it is derived from the client's cwd, which the shared server can now resolve reliably (chg:a-shared-client-outside-the-project-attaches-to-the-running-server). Implementation facts are measured against THAT root and held WITH that branch: an overlay per branch over the shared intent, or a branch tag on the node. They reach main when, and only because, the branch's code merges. Intent writes stay live for everyone. Needs: a rule that says which node types and edges are branch-scoped (a classification like capture-intent's routing table, decided once, per rule:the-taxonomy-is-decided-once style), and what a session on main sees of open branches' overlays (probably: nothing, or a clearly labelled "in flight on branch X").
② THE SAVED DESIGN MERGES CORRECTLY UNDER GIT'S ORDINARY MERGE, so design and code merge in the same act, anywhere, GitHub included, without a custom driver. Today one file carries a whole-file content_hash and prev_content_hash; every export rewrites those lines, so ANY two PRs touching the design conflict textually even when their changes are disjoint. Options: (a) one file per node, or per node type, so disjoint changes touch disjoint files; (b) keep one file but move the chain out of it into a separate lineage record; (c) both. Lineage then has to be redesigned to match: per-item hashes, or lean on git's own history instead of a parallel chain. dec:export-once-per-pr and dec:export-serialisation-belongs-to-the-gate were built for the single-file chain and would change with it.
③ SEPARATE, NOT PART OF THIS: claim liveness reading `gone` for active sessions (fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22). It needs its own root-cause pass, but it bears on the same two-session case.

═══ REJECTED WITHIN THE BRAINSTORM, WITH THE REASON ═══
A GitHub Action that runs the merge driver on design conflicts: it hides the cause (every PR pair conflicts) rather than removing it. Anthony's stated preference is the correct fix.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══
🛑 THE BOUNDARY BETWEEN INTENT AND IMPLEMENTATION FACT IS NOT ALWAYS CLEAN. A capability's status moving to `realized` is intent-shaped but only true on the branch whose code realizes it. A verification's pass is a fact about a build. The classification in ① must handle "intent whose TRUTH depends on a branch", or it will mis-route exactly the records the gate cares about.
🛑 WHAT A SESSION ON MAIN SEES OF IN-FLIGHT BRANCHES is a product question. Invisible means a second branch can repeat the first's work; visible means "live" includes unmerged claims. Today's claims are the nearest existing answer, and they are broken (③).
🛑 SPLITTING THE FILE (②a) CHANGES WHAT EVERY CONSUMER COMMITS. flo2 and every installed project carry one docs/design/<project>.json; the CI gate, reflow2_init, the merge driver, and import/export all assume one document. It is a migration, not a flag.
⚠️ REPLACING THE WHOLE-FILE CHAIN touches settled history-integrity decisions (dec:export-once-per-pr; fact:a-broken-export-lineage-is-invisible-to-git-and-the-merge-driver-repaired-it). The chain exists so the design has a history independent of git. The replacement must keep that property, not just remove the conflict.
⚠️ dec:multi-writer-architecture (accepted: many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull, no hosted service) is CONSISTENT with this. It still means files in the repo, merged by git. But ② changes what "the repo file" is.

═══ SIZE, AS INFORMATION ═══
Large. ① is new server behaviour plus a classification decision. ② is a storage-format migration across reflow2 and every consumer, with lineage redesigned.
